I love how clean this feels. That is really the only way I can put it. I was able to get a few games that I had in my steam library installed. Unfortunately, I can't get them all. I got Ark working and I got Minecraft (not steam) working with the FTB launcher. If I could get Elite Dangerous or Space Engineers working I would be mostly set as far as what I am currently playing. I also cannot connect to my work VPN just yet, although, I did get the client installed. I still have hope that I can work through that sticking point.

For the time being, I will have to keep dual boot. Also, until i get the VPN situation sorted out, I will have to log into work via the Windows desktop.

The final thing on my to-do list is to nuke my system and do a clean win 7 install, and then reinstall Linux. The problem is, when I removed Grub and repaired my Boot sector, it left a 100mb partition at the front of my C drive. Since it is the first partition, I cannot expand it into either the windows or Linux partitions.

My primary hard drive is a 250gb SSD. I have a 1TB drive for my files. This is where my games and music and stuff are, I wont have to touch that, but I really want to reduce the room I am taking up with Windows and give more to the Linux.

I will admit, I keep getting tripped up on some things. I expect certain things to work how I would do it in Windows, but find out that it just doesn't. I am somewhat excited about using the terminal more. It reminds me of what it was like in the 80's on my old AT&T.

To that point, the big thing that I have noticed is that I am logging in more to interact with the PC.
